The story has a strong underlying unity where the plot, setting, and character arcs seamlessly interweave. The beginning establishes the central conflict: two people accustomed to temporary lives and contracts ("six-week increments of borrowed rooms") who are avoiding the topic of what happens "after" their residency ends. The middle uses the physical setting of the beach and the incoming tide as a literal and metaphorical trap, forcing them to be "genuinely, physically, mutually stuck" so they can no longer avoid confessing their feelings and future plans (Iowa and Boston). Small details introduced early on—like the borrowed equipment, the check-engine light, and the tide chart in the ziplock bag—are carried through to the end, culminating in a logical, emotionally resonant conclusion that directly resolves the opening tension about their temporary status.
